items.main_sentence: «This world is a passage, and the Hereafter is home; what we truly seek belongs in our homeland.»
items.explanation: This world is a stage on a journey, not the final destination. Wealth and pleasures are used to meet one’s needs, while one’s efforts are directed towards what will benefit a person after death, just as a traveller does not make the road a permanent home.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«This world is a passage, and the Hereafter is home; what we truly seek belongs in our homeland.»
Al-Fawāʾid

This world is a stage on a journey, not the final destination. Wealth and pleasures are used to meet one’s needs, while one’s efforts are directed towards what will benefit a person after death, just as a traveller does not make the road a permanent home.

arabic.main_sentence: «الدنيا مجاز والآخرة وطن والأوطار إنما تطلب في الأوطان.»
arabic.explanation: الدنيا مرحلة عبور وليست الغاية النهائية؛ فالمال والمتع يؤخذ منها قدر الحاجة، ويكون العمل موجّهًا إلى ما ينفع الإنسان بعد الموت، كما لا يتخذ المسافر الطريق وطنًا.

items.main_sentence: «When hearts turn away from the banquets of this world, they sit at the banquets of the Hereafter among those invited; when they settle for this world's banquets, they miss the others.»
items.explanation: The tables of this world represent pleasures that may distract a person from Allah; the tables of the Hereafter represent what He has prepared for those who turn to Him. Attachment to the former can cause the latter to be forgotten.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«When hearts turn away from the banquets of this world, they sit at the banquets of the Hereafter among those invited; when they settle for this world's banquets, they miss the others.»
Al-Fawāʾid

The tables of this world represent pleasures that may distract a person from Allah; the tables of the Hereafter represent what He has prepared for those who turn to Him. Attachment to the former can cause the latter to be forgotten.

arabic.main_sentence: «إذا زهدت القلوب في موائد الدنيا قعدت على موائد الآخرة بين أهل تلك الدعوة، وإذا رضيت بموائد الدنيا فاتتها تلك الموائد.»
arabic.explanation: موائد الدنيا ترمز إلى الملذات التي قد تشغل عن الله، وموائد الآخرة إلى ما أعدّه للمقبلين عليه؛ والتعلق بالأولى قد يُنسي الثانية.

items.main_sentence: «Whoever's heart is filled with love and reverence for God does not consider what they gave up of this world for His sake worthy of being called a sacrifice.»
items.explanation: A person who gives up a pleasure or advantage to seek Allah’s pleasure does not regard the sacrifice as something immense. Closeness to Allah is worth far more than whatever worldly benefit was relinquished.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«Whoever's heart is filled with love and reverence for God does not consider what they gave up of this world for His sake worthy of being called a sacrifice.»
Madārij as-Sālikīn

A person who gives up a pleasure or advantage to seek Allah’s pleasure does not regard the sacrifice as something immense. Closeness to Allah is worth far more than whatever worldly benefit was relinquished.

arabic.main_sentence: «فإن من امتلأ قلبه بمحبة الله وتعظيمه لا يرى أن ما تركه لأجله من الدنيا يستحق أن يجعل قربانا.»
arabic.explanation: من ترك متعة أو مصلحة طلبًا لرضا الله لا يستعظم ما ضحّى به؛ فقيمة القرب من الله أعظم من قيمة ما تركه من الدنيا.

items.main_sentence: «Power, status, wealth and even spiritual states are given to the righteous and the wicked, to believers and unbelievers alike.»
items.explanation: Wealth and influence can belong to people who are not righteous. Worldly success alone therefore does not establish that Allah is pleased with the person who enjoys it.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«Power, status, wealth and even spiritual states are given to the righteous and the wicked, to believers and unbelievers alike.»
Madārij as-Sālikīn
Wealth and influence can belong to people who are not righteous. Worldly success alone therefore does not establish that Allah is pleased with the person who enjoys it.

arabic.main_sentence: «فإن الملك والجاه والمال والحال معطاة للبر والفاجر، والمؤمن والكافر.»
arabic.explanation: الغنى والنفوذ قد يجتمعان مع عدم الصلاح؛ لذلك لا يدل النجاح الدنيوي وحده على رضا الله عن صاحبه.

items.main_sentence: «People differ in their aspirations, not in their outward appearances.»
items.explanation: True distinction lies not in appearance or fame, but in the nobility of a person’s aims and the effort devoted to doing good.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«People differ in their aspirations, not in their outward appearances.»
Al-Fawāʾid
True distinction lies not in appearance or fame, but in the nobility of a person’s aims and the effort devoted to doing good.

arabic.main_sentence: «إنما تفاوت القوم بالهمم لا بالصور.»
arabic.explanation: التفاضل الحقيقي لا يقوم على المظهر أو الشهرة، وإنما على علوّ المقاصد والجهد المبذول في تحقيق الخير.

items.main_sentence: «When God wishes good for a servant, He makes them acknowledge their own sins, refrain from dwelling on others’ sins, give generously from what they have, avoid coveting others’ possessions, and patiently bear harm from others.»
items.explanation: Acknowledging one’s own faults is the beginning of self-reform, unlike preoccupation with the faults of others. This goes together with being generous to others from what one has, without coveting what they possess.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim

«When God wishes good for a servant, He makes them acknowledge their own sins, refrain from dwelling on others’ sins, give generously from what they have, avoid coveting others’ possessions, and patiently bear harm from others.»
Al-Fawāʾid

Acknowledging one’s own faults is the beginning of self-reform, unlike preoccupation with the faults of others. This goes together with being generous to others from what one has, without coveting what they possess.

arabic.main_sentence: «إذا أراد الله بعبد خيرا جعله معترفا بذنبه ممسكا عن ذنب غيره، جوادا بما عنده، زاهدا فيما عند غيره، محتملا لأذى غيره.»
arabic.explanation: الاعتراف بالخطأ بداية إصلاح النفس، بخلاف الانشغال بتتبع أخطاء الآخرين؛ ويقترن ذلك بالإحسان إليهم بما يملكه المرء من غير طمع فيما عندهم.

items.main_sentence: «A deed without sincerity and without following prophetic guidance is like a traveler filling a bag with sand: it weighs them down but brings no benefit.»
items.explanation: A large number of deeds is of no benefit if their purpose is to win people’s praise or if they run contrary to the Prophet’s ﷺ guidance. Their value depends on sincerity and on following his example.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«A deed without sincerity and without following prophetic guidance is like a traveler filling a bag with sand: it weighs them down but brings no benefit.»
Al-Fawāʾid
A large number of deeds is of no benefit if their purpose is to win people’s praise or if they run contrary to the Prophet’s ﷺ guidance. Their value depends on sincerity and on following his example.

arabic.main_sentence: «العمل بغير إخلاص ولا اقتداء كالمسافر يملأ جرابه رملا يثقله ولا ينفعه.»
arabic.explanation: كثرة الأعمال وحدها لا تنفع إذا كان المقصود منها مدح الناس أو كانت مخالفة لهدي النبي ﷺ؛ فقيمتها مرتبطة بالإخلاص والاتباع.

items.main_sentence: «The most beneficial deed is one in which sincerity makes you forget people's attention, and awareness of God's favor makes you forget your own merit; you focus neither on yourself nor on others.»
items.explanation: Sincerity frees good deeds from the expectation of people’s praise, while recognising Allah’s favour prevents self-admiration. The very ability to do good is itself a blessing from Him.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«The most beneficial deed is one in which sincerity makes you forget people's attention, and awareness of God's favor makes you forget your own merit; you focus neither on yourself nor on others.»
Al-Fawāʾid
Sincerity frees good deeds from the expectation of people’s praise, while recognising Allah’s favour prevents self-admiration. The very ability to do good is itself a blessing from Him.

arabic.main_sentence: «أنفع العمل أن تغيب فيه عن الناس بالإخلاص وعن نفسك بشهود المنة، فلا ترى فيه نفسك ولا ترى الخلق.»
arabic.explanation: الإخلاص يحرر عمل الخير من انتظار ثناء الناس، وشهود منّة الله يمنع العجب بالنفس؛ فالقدرة على فعل الخير نفسها نعمة منه.

items.main_sentence: «Whoever knows their own self becomes occupied with correcting it rather than finding fault with others.»
items.explanation: Awareness of one’s own faults and of what needs to be put right leaves less room for scrutinising other people’s shortcomings and passing judgment on them.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«Whoever knows their own self becomes occupied with correcting it rather than finding fault with others.»
Al-Fawāʾid
Awareness of one’s own faults and of what needs to be put right leaves less room for scrutinising other people’s shortcomings and passing judgment on them.

arabic.main_sentence: «من عرف نفسه اشتغل بإصلاحها عن عيوب الناس.»
arabic.explanation: معرفة الإنسان بأخطائه وما يحتاج إلى إصلاحه تقلل انشغاله بمراقبة عيوب غيره والحكم عليهم.

items.main_sentence: «God has spared us competition over this world's fleeting gains by inviting us to compete for the Hereafter and what He has prepared there.»
items.explanation: Beneficial competition concerns deeds whose good endures into the Hereafter, such as seeking knowledge and giving charity, rather than comparing one’s wealth and standing with those of others.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«God has spared us competition over this world's fleeting gains by inviting us to compete for the Hereafter and what He has prepared there.»
Ighāthat al-Lahfān
Beneficial competition concerns deeds whose good endures into the Hereafter, such as seeking knowledge and giving charity, rather than comparing one’s wealth and standing with those of others.

arabic.main_sentence: «أغنانا عن طلب التنافس في الدنيا وعاجلها بما أحبه لنا وندبنا إليه من التنافس في الآخرة وما أعد لنا فيها.»
arabic.explanation: التنافس النافع يكون في الأعمال التي تنفع في الآخرة، كالعلم والصدقة، بدل الانشغال بمقارنة المال والمكانة بما عند الآخرين.

items.main_sentence: «The more someone knows God and His attributes, the sounder and stronger their reliance on Him becomes.»
items.explanation: The more a person knows Allah, His names and His attributes, and the more certain they become of His power, wisdom, mercy and His management of all affairs, the stronger their reliance on Him becomes and the more reassurance their heart finds in His choice. This is because they know that their affairs are in the hands of a Lord who is all-knowing, wise and merciful, and for whom nothing is beyond His power.

«The more someone knows God and His attributes, the sounder and stronger their reliance on Him becomes.»

This is because they know that their affairs are in the hands of a Lord who is all-knowing, wise and merciful, and for whom nothing is beyond His power.

arabic.main_sentence: «فكل من كان بالله وصفاته أعلم وأعرف كان توكله أصح وأقوى.»
arabic.explanation: كلما ازداد الإنسان معرفةً بالله وأسمائه وصفاته، وازداد يقينًا بقدرته وحكمته ورحمته وتدبيره، قوي اعتماده عليه واطمأن قلبه إلى اختياره، لأنه يعلم أن أموره بيد ربٍّ عليمٍ حكيمٍ رحيمٍ لا يعجزه شيء.

items.main_sentence: «Entrusting matters to God means placing all your affairs before Him willingly and by choice, not reluctantly or only out of necessity.»
items.explanation: Entrusting one’s affairs to Allah means choosing from the outset to place them in His care and seek His help, rather than turning to Him only after other attempts have failed. It combines earnest effort with leaving to Allah those outcomes that lie beyond human control.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«Entrusting matters to God means placing all your affairs before Him willingly and by choice, not reluctantly or only out of necessity.»
Madārij as-Sālikīn

Entrusting one’s affairs to Allah means choosing from the outset to place them in His care and seek His help, rather than turning to Him only after other attempts have failed. It combines earnest effort with leaving to Allah those outcomes that lie beyond human control.

arabic.main_sentence: التفويض: «إلقاء أموره كلها إلى الله، وإنزالها به طلبًا واختيارًا، لا كرهًا واضطرارًا.»
arabic.explanation: تفويض الأمر إلى الله يكون باختيار العبد أن يكل أمره إليه، مع طلب عونه منذ البداية، لا بمجرد اللجوء إليه بعد فشل المحاولات؛ وهو يجتمع مع الاجتهاد وترك ما لا يملكه الإنسان من النتائج لله.

items.main_sentence: The fruit of true reliance: «When a person genuinely trusts God, they accept what He chooses for them.»
items.explanation: True reliance on Allah is shown by continuing to trust Him after making every effort, even when the hoped-for outcome does not occur. Such trust is not conditional on one’s wishes being fulfilled.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
The fruit of true reliance: «When a person genuinely trusts God, they accept what He chooses for them.»
Madārij as-Sālikīn
True reliance on Allah is shown by continuing to trust Him after making every effort, even when the hoped-for outcome does not occur. Such trust is not conditional on one’s wishes being fulfilled.

arabic.main_sentence: ثمرة التوكل: «فإنه إذا توكل حق التوكل رضي بما يفعله وكيله.»
arabic.explanation: صدق التوكل يظهر في بقاء الثقة بالله بعد بذل الجهد، حتى عندما لا تتحقق النتيجة المرجوة؛ فلا تكون هذه الثقة مشروطة بتحقق الرغبات.

items.main_sentence: «Reliance on God is a state of the heart born of knowing Him and believing that He alone creates and governs, brings harm and benefit, and gives and withholds.»
items.explanation: Taking practical steps, such as working or seeking medical treatment, goes together with recognising that the results are not in human hands alone and seeking Allah’s help in attaining them.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«Reliance on God is a state of the heart born of knowing Him and believing that He alone creates and governs, brings harm and benefit, and gives and withholds.»
Madārij as-Sālikīn
Taking practical steps, such as working or seeking medical treatment, goes together with recognising that the results are not in human hands alone and seeking Allah’s help in attaining them.

arabic.main_sentence: التوكل: «هو حال للقلب ينشأ عن معرفته بالله، والإيمان بتفرده بالخلق والتدبير والضر والنفع، والعطاء والمنع.»
arabic.explanation: الأخذ بالأسباب، كالعمل أو العلاج، يجتمع مع إدراك أن النتائج ليست بيد الإنسان وحده، ومع طلب العون من الله عليها.

items.main_sentence: «A servant's love for their Lord surpasses every love that can be measured; other loves cannot compare with it.»
items.explanation: Love for one’s family and for the things of this world is natural. When a desire conflicts with Allah’s command, however, obedience to Him takes precedence.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«A servant's love for their Lord surpasses every love that can be measured; other loves cannot compare with it.»
Madārij as-Sālikīn
Love for one’s family and for the things of this world is natural. When a desire conflicts with Allah’s command, however, obedience to Him takes precedence.

arabic.main_sentence: «محبة العبد لربه فوق كل محبة تقدر، ولا نسبة لسائر المحاب إليها.»
arabic.explanation: محبة الأهل وما يُحب من أمور الدنيا أمر طبيعي، لكن طاعة الله تتقدم عندما تتعارض الرغبة مع أمره.

items.main_sentence: «Hearts are naturally inclined to love those who have been kind to them.»
items.explanation: Reflecting on familiar blessings, such as health, security and the love of family, renews awareness of their value. Recognising Allah’s kindness increases love for Him in the heart.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«Hearts are naturally inclined to love those who have been kind to them.»
Madārij as-Sālikīn
Reflecting on familiar blessings, such as health, security and the love of family, renews awareness of their value. Recognising Allah’s kindness increases love for Him in the heart.

arabic.main_sentence: «فإن القلوب مجبولة على حب من أحسن إليها.»
arabic.explanation: التأمل في نعم مألوفة، كالصحة والأمان ومحبة الأهل، يعيد إدراك قيمتها؛ ومعرفة إحسان الله تزيد محبته في القلب.

items.main_sentence: A sincere lover finds companionship with God among people just as they find it in solitude.
items.explanation: The comfort found in closeness to Allah is not confined to solitude. It also extends to remembering and obeying Him at work and among other people.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
A sincere lover finds companionship with God among people just as they find it in solitude.
Al-Fawāʾid (paraphrased)
The comfort found in closeness to Allah is not confined to solitude. It also extends to remembering and obeying Him at work and among other people.

arabic.main_sentence: المحب الصادق من وجد أنسه بالله بين الناس ووجده في الوحدة.
arabic.explanation: الأنس بالله لا يقتصر على الخلوة، بل يمتد إلى حفظ ذكره وطاعته في العمل وبين الناس.

items.main_sentence: «Complete delight, joy, a good life and bliss are found in knowing God, affirming His oneness, feeling close to Him, longing to meet Him and directing the heart toward Him.»
items.explanation: The joy brought by wealth or success may fade. Knowing Allah and finding closeness to Him through worship give life a meaning that does not depend on such gains.
items.source: Risālat Ibn al-Qayyim ilā Aḥad Ikhwānih

arabic.main_sentence: «اللذة التامة والفرح والسرور وطيب العيش والنعيم إنما هو في معرفة الله وتوحيده والأنس به والشوق إلى لقائه واجتماع القلب والهم عليه.»
arabic.explanation: الفرح بالمال أو النجاح قد يزول أثره، أما معرفة الله والأنس بعبادته فيمنحان الحياة معنى لا يتوقف على هذه المكاسب.

items.main_sentence: «Repentance for a sin must be undertaken immediately; it must not be delayed.»
items.explanation: Repentance is not postponed until a convenient time. It entails abandoning the sin, regretting it and resolving not to return to it, as well as restoring the rights of others where required.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«Repentance for a sin must be undertaken immediately; it must not be delayed.»
Madārij as-Sālikīn
Repentance is not postponed until a convenient time. It entails abandoning the sin, regretting it and resolving not to return to it, as well as restoring the rights of others where required.

arabic.main_sentence: «المبادرة إلى التوبة من الذنب فرض على الفور، ولا يجوز تأخيرها.»
arabic.explanation: التوبة لا تؤخر إلى وقت ملائم؛ بل تقتضي ترك الذنب والندم عليه والعزم على عدم العودة إليه، مع رد الحقوق إن لزمت.

items.main_sentence: «Repentance is among the greatest good deeds.»
items.explanation: Repentance is not a reason for self-admiration, but a blessing that calls for gratitude to Allah for enabling the return to Him, along with continued efforts to remedy one’s shortcomings.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«Repentance is among the greatest good deeds.»
Madārij as-Sālikīn

arabic.main_sentence: «فإن التوبة من أعظم الحسنات.»
arabic.explanation: التوبة ليست سببًا للعجب بالنفس، بل نعمة تستدعي شكر الله على توفيقه للرجوع إليه، والاستمرار في إصلاح التقصير.

items.main_sentence: «The heart falls ill as the body does: repentance and restraint heal it; it rusts as a mirror does, and remembrance of God polishes it.»
items.explanation: Just as an ill person needs medicine and must avoid what worsens the illness, the heart needs repentance, remembrance of Allah and distance from whatever draws it back into sin.

readingParts.text: Ibn al-Qayyim
«The heart falls ill as the body does: repentance and restraint heal it; it rusts as a mirror does, and remembrance of God polishes it.»

Just as an ill person needs medicine and must avoid what worsens the illness, the heart needs repentance, remembrance of Allah and distance from whatever draws it back into sin.

arabic.main_sentence: «القلب يمرض كما يمرض البدن وشفاؤه في التوبة والحمية، ويصدأ كما تصدأ المرآة وجلاؤه بالذكر.»
arabic.explanation: كما يحتاج المريض إلى الدواء وتجنب ما يزيد مرضه، يحتاج القلب إلى التوبة والابتعاد عما يعيد إلى الذنب، وإلى ذكر الله.

items.main_sentence: «If you want to benefit from the Qur'an, give it your full attention while reciting or listening to it.»
items.explanation: Benefiting from the Quran requires attention to its meanings and an understanding of what Allah asks of His servant. Simply making the completion of pages one’s sole concern does not achieve this.

arabic.main_sentence: «إذا أردت الانتفاع بالقرآن فاجمع قلبك عند تلاوته وسماعه.»
arabic.explanation: الانتفاع بالقرآن يتطلب الانتباه إلى معانيه وفهم ما يطلبه الله من العبد، ولا يتحقق بمجرد جعل إنهاء الصفحات هو الهمّ الوحيد.

items.main_sentence: «Whoever knows the value of what they seek finds it easier to bear what they must give for it.»
items.explanation: Remembering the hope of Allah’s pleasure and reward makes it easier to persevere in obedience, even when doing so requires effort and patience.

items.main_sentence: «Provision and lifespan are paired and guaranteed: as long as one's appointed time remains, provision will come.»

arabic.main_sentence: «الرزق والأجل قرينان مضمونان، فما دام الأجل باقيا كان الرزق آتيا.»
arabic.explanation: السعي في طلب الرزق لا يقتضي أن يدفع الخوف من المستقبل إلى الحرام؛ فالرزق الذي يصل إلى الإنسان إنما يصل بتقدير الله.

items.main_sentence: «Whoever seeks a livelihood with moderation finds relief from the misery and worries of this world.»
items.explanation: A sound approach to earning a livelihood combines diligence with lawful means, without sacrificing health and peace of mind to an endless pursuit of more money.

items.main_sentence: «When God, in His wisdom, closes one path of provision to you, He, in His mercy, opens another that is better for you.»

arabic.main_sentence: «إذا سد عليك بحكمته طريقا من طرقه فتح لك برحمته طريقا أنفع لك منه.»

items.main_sentence: «Whoever wants a pure heart should prefer God over their desires.»

arabic.main_sentence: «من أراد صفاء قلبه فليؤثر الله على شهوته.»

items.main_sentence: «Hearts attached to desires are kept from God in proportion to that attachment.»

items.main_sentence: «The soul sometimes desires what harms it because it does not know the harm, sometimes because its intentions are corrupt, and sometimes because of both.»

arabic.main_sentence: «فالنفس تهوى ما يضرها ولا ينفعها لجهلها بمضرته لها تارة، ولفساد قصدها تارة، ولمجموعهما تارة.»

items.main_sentence: «Whoever makes their heart's home with their Lord finds calm and rest; whoever sends it wandering among people becomes unsettled and anxious.»

arabic.main_sentence: «من وطن قلبه عند ربه سكن واستراح، ومن أرسله في الناس اضطرب واشتد به القلق.»
